newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia eyes extending VAT, cutting rates.
newsitem.headline: Colombia eyes extending VAT, cutting rates.

text.p: Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Monday he was considering cutting the sales tax from the current rate of 16 percent but extending it to a wider range of goods and services.
"We're studying a proposal to reduce Value Added Tax (VAT) but eliminate almost all exemptions," Ocampo told a press conference.
He said such a move would make the tax simpler and fairer to apply and would potentially cut the level of tax evasion.
But Ocampo added that the government still had doubts as to whether such a cut would result in more or less revenues.
The proposal was submitted by members of the ruling Liberal Party after Colombia's constitutional court ruled that the state of emergency declared by the government in January was illegal.
The state of emergency was designed to rein in the government's yawning fiscal deficit which was running at about four percent of gross domestic product in 1996.
